cards.title: Introduction to Configuration
cards.content: ASP.NET Core provides a robust configuration system based on key-value pairs. These values can be loaded from various sources at runtime, including JSON files, environment variables, command-line arguments, and Azure Key Vault.

cards.title: appsettings.json Structure
cards.content:
The default configuration source is usually appsettings.json located in the project root.

{
  "Logging": {
    "LogLevel": {
      "Default": "Information"
    }
  },
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    "DefaultConnection": "Server=(localdb)\mssqllocaldb;Database=TestDb;"
  }
}

cards.title: Accessing Configuration with IConfiguration
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core uses Dependency Injection to provide access to configuration values via the IConfiguration interface.

public class HomeController : Controller
{
    private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;

    public HomeController(IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        _configuration = configuration;
    }

    public IActionResult Index()
    {
        string connString = _configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection");
        return View();
    }
}

cards.title: The Options Pattern
cards.content:
The Options pattern uses C# classes to strongly type and strongly validate configuration settings. This avoids using magic strings throughout your codebase.

public class SmtpSettings
{
    public string Host { get; set; }
    public int Port { get; set; }
}

// Registered in Program.cs
builder.Services.Configure<SmtpSettings>(builder.Configuration.GetSection("Smtp"));

cards.title: Injecting Configuration
cards.content: To access configuration settings in a service via Dependency Injection, you request the interface named [blank].

cards.title: Environment Variables & Overrides
cards.content: ASP.NET Core allows configuration providers to override values based on precedence. Environment variables typically override appsettings.json settings. To use environment-specific settings, use files like appsettings.Development.json or appsettings.Production.json.

cards.title: Match Configuration Providers to their Syntax

content.instructions: Order the configuration sources from lowest precedence to highest precedence (later sources override earlier ones in the default setup).

cards.title: Configuration Summary
cards.content: You have learned how ASP.NET Core handles configuration using hierarchical JSON files, environment variables, the IConfiguration interface, and strongly-typed settings using the Options pattern.
